findings.title: Shell command construction does not escape arguments
findings.description: `get_cli_string()` inserts `path`, `key`, and most `value` inputs directly into a string documented as suitable for execution by a shell. A value such as `$(...)` is interpolated by the shell even without spaces; paths and keys can also inject shell syntax. Adding double quotes only when a value contains spaces does not make it safe, since quotes, substitutions, and backslashes are not escaped.
findings.suggestion: Avoid constructing shell commands as strings where possible; return an argument list for subprocess use. If shell text is required, quote every argument with a shell-aware quoting function such as `shlex.quote` and document the shell-specific behavior.

findings.title: Export-mode output is not safe to source as a shell script
findings.description: `set_key()` writes the key verbatim and escapes apostrophes in values with a backslash, then wraps the value in single quotes. Backslash does not escape an apostrophe inside a POSIX shell single-quoted string, so a value containing an apostrophe can terminate the quote and inject shell commands when the resulting `export` file is sourced. An attacker-controlled key can also inject shell syntax. This affects the CLI's `--export` mode, which describes the output as an executable Bash script.
findings.suggestion: Use a shell-specific serializer for export output, safely quote values, and validate keys as shell identifiers. Keep dotenv-file serialization separate from shell-script serialization.

findings.title: Documented uv lint and format commands are invalid
findings.description: The instructions run `uv ruff check .` and `uv format .`, but uv does not provide these subcommands. Following the documented test instructions therefore stops before linting/formatting.
findings.suggestion: Use `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format .` (or the equivalent commands through the project's chosen environment).

findings.title: Documented uv lint and format commands are invalid
findings.description: This duplicated guide also instructs contributors to run `uv ruff check .` and `uv format .`; these are not valid uv subcommands, so the documented workflow fails.
findings.suggestion: Use `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format .` and keep this copy synchronized with the root contributing guide.

findings.title: CLI get treats an existing empty value as a missing key
findings.description: `get()` checks `if stored_value`, so a key present as `KEY=` is treated as absent and exits with status 1 without printing the empty value. The key exists; the check should distinguish `None` from an empty string.
findings.suggestion: Check `stored_value is not None` and add a CLI test for retrieving a key whose value is empty.

findings.title: List test uses the built-in format instead of the parameter
findings.description: The condition `if format is not None` refers to Python's built-in `format` function, which is always non-None, rather than the `output_format` parameter. For the case where `output_format` is `None`, the test passes `--format None` and Click rejects it, so the expected default-format case fails.
findings.suggestion: Change the condition to `if output_format is not None` and run the test suite to confirm the default-format case.

findings.title: Tests change the process working directory without restoring it
findings.description: The IPython tests call `os.chdir(tmp_path)` directly. The process-wide working directory then leaks into subsequent tests, making behavior dependent on test ordering and potentially leaving the suite in a temporary directory.
findings.suggestion: Use pytest's `monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)` fixture so the original working directory is restored after each test; apply the same approach to other tests that call `os.chdir` directly.

findings.title: Unused documentation dependency
findings.description: `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` is declared here, but `mkdocs.yml` does not configure the `include-markdown` plugin and the provided documentation does not use its directives. It adds an unnecessary package to documentation setup.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dependency if it is no longer needed, or configure and use the plugin if its omission is accidental.

findings.title: Parser reads the entire input into memory before parsing
findings.description: `Reader.__init__()` calls `stream.read()` without a bound, retaining the complete input string before producing any bindings. Large dotenv files—or a FIFO that continues producing data—can consume excessive memory and delay processing until EOF.
findings.suggestion: Consider parsing incrementally from the stream, or impose and document a reasonable input-size limit, especially for FIFO input.

findings.title: Debug print remains in test helper
findings.description: `setup_zipfile()` prints every generated `__init__.py` path. This is leftover diagnostic output that can clutter test output when capture is disabled.
findings.suggestion: Remove the print or replace it with logging that is enabled only when explicitly requested.
